verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego... at 8:07 p.m. ET, right on schedule.'; R2: 'splashdown around 8:07 p.m.... off the coast of San Diego.'; R3: 'water landing around 8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact location, date, and approximate time of splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission had a crew of four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the four Artemis II astronauts'; R2: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'the four astronauts'; R4: 'the four astronauts'.
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state or list the four crew members.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'historic 10-day trip to the moon... after 10 days in space'; R4: 'historic 10-day Artemis II mission'; R6: '10-day mission'; R7: 'record-breaking 10-day mission'; R9: 'historic 10-day mission'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe it as a 10-day mission, though precise duration is ~9 days 1 hour; common approximation directly supports claim.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission went around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'flyby around the moon... looping around the Earth and moon... circled around the moon'; R3: 'journey toward our celestial neighbor... swung by the moon'; R4: 'around the far side of the moon'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm lunar flyby or circumnavigation.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew was recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'flown to the flight deck of USS John P. Murtha'; R2: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'airlifted onto a U.S. Navy recovery vessel... USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'USS John P. Murtha'.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly name the USS John P. Murtha as the recovery ship.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is safe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'all four members of the crew were "feeling great, happy to be home"'; R4: 'all four crew members are safe and well'; R7: '"Four green crew members"'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly report crew in good condition post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is returning to Houston for post-mission evaluations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'undergo post‑mission medical evaluations before... bound for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston'; R3: 'board an aircraft bound for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston'; R1: 'post-splashdown news conference Friday night from Houston'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm transport to Houston (Johnson Space Center) for medical evaluations.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II 10-day flight tested systems to prepare for future human moon landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'paving the way for a potential moon landing in 2028... tested out their gear'; R5: 'test flight for future lunar landings'; R7: 'vital test flight that will set the stage for a moon landing'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as a test mission preparing for future lunar landings; 10-day supported as above.
